Source reconstruction from the configured Windows PE instruction bytes.
Steam image PE:6a70a6d9:02711000; classic image PE:6a70b91c:0270a000.
These files describe native source construction, not a gameplay observation.

The screenshot instruction identifies announcement_alert_interfacest::render:
Steam 0x40d5f0..0x40f77a; classic 0x40b1b0..0x40d33a.
The whole function and input function were read from both installed images.

Source branch precedence is:
  if owner.viewing_unit != null:
    iterate owner.viewing_unit.unit_announcement_ids[owner.viewing_unit_uac];
    locate each ID in world.status.reports;
    absent report ID: skip that entry;
    present ID: wrap complete report.text from report+8.
  else if owner.viewing_alert_button:
    iterate world.status.alert_button_announcement_id;
    locate each ID in world.status.reports;
    absent report ID: skip that entry;
    present ID: wrap complete report.text from report+8.
  else if owner.viewing_alert != null:
    iterate viewing_alert.announcement_id (alert+8);
    locate each ID in world.status.reports;
    absent report ID: skip that entry;
    present ID: wrap complete report.text from report+8;
    then iterate the parallel alert.report_unid and category vectors;
    absent unit: skip the unit summary (popup has no Somebody fallback);
    present unit: construct the category summary below.
  else:
    draw no body source.

At every report path, repeat_count <= 0 uses report.text unchanged.
At every report path, repeat_count > 0 copies report.text, appends " x",
then appends the signed int32 result of repeat_count+1 in decimal.
The first relevant Steam instructions are 0x40d812/0x40d82c,
0x40dc7f/0x40dc99 and 0x40e0a0/0x40e0ba. Classic report starts are
0x40b3d2/0x40b3ec, 0x40b83f/0x40b859 and 0x40bc60/0x40bc7a.
Neither wrapping nor the repeat suffix creates a second semantic message.
The renderer retains the complete report pointer beside every native row.

Popup unit-summary construction (Steam 0x40e48d..0x40e50e):
  identity = unit::full-name/profession formatter 0x1331500;
  capitalize(identity), append " is ";
  category == 0: append "fighting!";
  category == 1: append "sparring.";
  category == 2: append "hunting.";
  all other category values: append no status text.
Thus the complete finite productions are:
  {unit-identity} is fighting!
  {unit-identity} is sparring.
  {unit-identity} is hunting.
  {unit-identity} is [native invalid category fallthrough]
The same formatter's modes 4/5 can copy a zero-length first_name and
return normally. The popup does not reject that empty native caption.
Capitalization here precedes appending " is ", so the additional complete
visible productions have lowercase initial letters:
  is fighting!
  is sparring.
  is hunting.
  is [native invalid category fallthrough]
Typed unit/category ownership plus equality to the entire cached summary
proves an empty label without inferring a missing character's name. The
three valid-category translations fill the existing {n} summary templates
with that exact empty caption. The invalid-category empty copula has no
activity meaning and contributes no translated ink. The hover reader also
retains a successful empty formatter result instead of rejecting its cache.
The hover renderer additionally uses "Somebody" when its unit lookup fails;
that fallback belongs to hover, not the selected-alert popup.

Fixed instruction productions (whole paragraph, including native spaces):
  viewing_unit != null, or viewing_alert_button, or selected alert without
  report_unid entries:
    You can recenter on certain announcements.  Right click to close.
  selected alert with report_unid entries:
    Select a report to view the full text.  Right click to close.
The full popup render body has no other authored UI sentence branch.
Its empty strings, minimum-three-row icon padding and graphic glyphs
contribute no additional translatable textual production.

The body therefore accepts complete report text from every native submit
producer admitted by the routing configuration, rather than one particular
revelation constructor or a prefix matched from announcement history.

Native report source ownership:
  Steam submission 0xe3c20..0xe569d / classic 0xe3bb0..0xe562d
  reads signed int16 announcement_infost.type at parameters+0;
  values below 0 or >= 356 return;
  the source NativeString is the second parameter;
  at Steam 0xe4680 a native report is allocated;
  at 0xe468a..0xe468f the exact type is copied into report+0;
  at 0xe4692..0xe46ad the complete source is copied into report.text at +8.
  Repeat coalescing compares the complete submitted source to report.text
  and increments report.repeat_count at +0x34 (Steam 0xe45f8..0xe47f8).
  Routing observes per-type announcement flags at init+0x1d0+type*4,
  an explicit alert-type mapping, and optional unit/category ownership.
  Alert report references always resolve those same stored complete records.

The deterministic report-to-alert-group helper has no unwind entry, so its
actual leaf code was read independently: Steam 0xeaa20..0xeab13 and classic
0xea9b0..0xeaaa3. It bounds the unsigned type at 353, reads the native byte
remap at Steam 0xeaba0 / classic 0xeab30, then the embedded RVA jump table
at Steam 0xeab14 / classic 0xeaaa4. Targets return alert groups 0..33.
Accepted announcement types 354 and 355 use the default GENERAL group 0.
native-announcement-alert-routing.tsv records each actual table target for
every one of the 356 types in both images. The submitter independently
adds unit/category ownership to combat, sparring and hunting alerts.

All decoded direct native submissions in the configured images:
  235 complete PE unwind functions per edition;
  712 actual direct call or cross-function tail-call instructions per edition.
  Every owner body, literal operand, decoded branch and switch is retained.
  native-submission-types.tsv reconstructs the parameters+0 branch values
  at each of the 1424 actual sites, preserving alternative values at shared
  tail calls instead of assuming the lexically preceding type write.
  native-announcement-enum.tsv retains all 356 accepted numeric values;
  symbolic enum labels are explicitly attributed to local df-structures.
  Some accepted enum values have no current static direct producer; that
  is not evidence for inventing additional caption sentences.

Typed/open data fields are retained as fields, not enumerated proper names:
  unit/historical-figure identity and profession;
  language_name, site/entity/artifact names;
  creature/caste/material/item/reaction/interaction RAW descriptions;
  authored dialogue/performance/written content;
  dates, counts, and recursive history-event text.
The complete reconstruction is the finite native source productions plus
those typed field suppliers. Runtime values and user-authored names can
create arbitrarily many complete report strings.

Native construction ownership is described by two complementary catalogs:
  native-production-catalog.tsv maps 165 reference owners to the existing
  complete English source catalogs and their exact native provenance.
  native-scoped-productions.tsv supplies the remaining 70 reference owners
  through complete report productions, recursively composed local clauses,
  and whole typed field suppliers. Two additional entries for owners
  0x10b150 and 0x110460 describe only their optional complete history_event
  subproduction; their arrival/rumor and invasion/commander main productions
  already belong to native-production-catalog.tsv. These two entries do not
  replace or summarize either complete owner body.
The union describes construction for all 235 actual reference submit owners.
native-producer-owners.tsv and native-submission-edges.tsv retain the paired
classic owners/sites, while both instruction dumps retain their branches,
literals and switches. A catalog owner denotes a native function with one
or more submissions, not one fixed sentence. Each owner can construct a
finite set of fixed messages, branch compositions, and open typed fields.
Announcement configuration and native alert/unit routing decide which
stored report reaches this popup; the renderer uses the same report.text.

native-fixed-producer-sources.tsv supplies the full-buffer constructions
that cannot be described by a nearby literal alone: action preconditions
returned by 0x85a8b0, slab writing copied from item+0xe8, written-work prose
returned by 0xcc7020/0xcc6a10 with their 0xcc5d50 continuation, complete
equipment messages, active RAW RETRACT_INTO_BP action expansion, and the
two EMBARK_MESSAGE documents. native-scoped-productions.tsv links these
supplier records to their runtime consumers. Stored titles, authored prose
and custom RAW action text remain supplier fields rather than invented
finite English expansions. These files describe source construction and
runtime ownership; they do not describe observed game display outcomes.

EMBARK_MESSAGE constructor 0x8b25a0..0x8b30e1 has exactly two submitted
document branches, both converging at 0x8b306a (type 342):
  second argument DL != 0 (0x8b27d3/0x8b27d5), or native state == 4
  (0x8b27db..0x8b27e4): return without an announcement;
  native state == 8 (0x8b2807/0x8b280a): revisit document
  0x8b284b..0x8b29b4, jumping to common submit at 0x8b29b9;
  every other admitted state: ordinary embark document
  0x8b29c4..0x8b2fe4, then common submit.
The revisit document contains its heading and two body paragraphs; the
ordinary document contains its heading/arrival, supplies, and site/strike
paragraphs. [B] and [C] are native paragraph/color controls, not additional
sentences. The original instruction paths and unsimplified documents are
in native-fixed-producer-sources.tsv; normalized complete compositions and
their local productions are in native-scoped-productions.tsv and runtime
announcement-combat-grammar.tsv (fortress-embark and embark-* scopes).

Both headings use entity race creature_raw.name[2] (+0x60), then native
capitalization. Missing entity supplies An. An entity with race < 0,
race outside the creature vector, or empty adjective supplies an empty
adjective after A, producing A  Outpost / A  Outpost Revisited; whitespace
normalization yields the separately authored A Outpost heading branches.
Ordinary supplies use race name[1] (+0x40), with charges for missing entity,
and a local dangerous creature plural or the explicit beasts fallback.
Entity race < 0/outside the vector leaves the race plural empty at
0x8b2bd1/0x8b2bf1 -> 0x8b2c22; empty RAW plurals likewise remain empty.
All three supplies compositions with one or both empty plural fields have
their own complete source productions. The invalid dangerous-species path
0x8b2e7b would dereference null+0x40 before submission; it is not an
additional completed announcement or a beasts fallback.
Civilization is the whole entity language_name or an empty field; site is
the native-name/quoted-English-name pair. The separate initial reclaim
interface constructor at 0x13797e0 has no direct submit site in the native
submit graph and contributes no additional document branch to this popup.

The 2026-10-19 disk-image re-read additionally retains actual Ghidra C output
for both complete render/input pairs in renderer/. Its three report sources,
repeat branches, two instruction sentences and unit/category summaries are
unchanged. This is source evidence, not an observation of the running game.

The NO_FISH producer at reference 0x13435b0 / classic 0x133e520 has been
expanded through every feature_init::getName virtual implementation and the
complete local/global selector in ../announcement-fishing/. The old {e}
place-name abstraction was incorrect: the virtual slot supplies ordinary
feature descriptions, not named waterbodies. The actual Ghidra output retains
74 finite productions and separate open material/owner/prefix compositions,
including empty fields and the unknown global-layer-type fallthrough.
adventure-announcements.tsv now owns the fixed descriptions/defaults and
adventure-announcement-grammar.tsv binds deposits to the existing material
supplier, with a separate owner-only form. The reloadable translations.tsv
has the same direct edits in the source workspace and both game installations;
no translation generator or build/deployment was run for this data change.
